regulatoryBasis: COBS 9.2.2R; COBS 9.2.5R; COBS 9A.2.18R where applicable; COBS 2.1.1R

queries.text: switch your existing pension into a new plan transfer the value across
encash surrender or close the existing policy
existing scheme advice retain switch transfer table
queries.note: Enumerates the ceding plans. Every plan with a non-Retain action needs its own instance of the groups below.

triggerProbe.presentWhen: At least one existing plan is being switched, transferred, encashed or surrendered.
triggerProbe.absentWhen: All existing plans are retained, or there are no existing plans.

queryGroups.requirement: Comparison of existing versus recommended product and investments

queries.text: comparison of your existing plan with the recommended scheme features charges fund range
pension switch analysis report existing scheme versus proposed scheme
number of funds available in the existing scheme and the new scheme
retirement options available flexi access drawdown UFPLS annuity in each scheme
whether the scheme allows a servicing adviser and adviser charge facilitation
performance of the existing fund compared with the recommended fund over five years
existing pension provision plans held provider policy number current value
queries.note: The fact find's own inventory of plans held. A plan tabulated in the report but absent from the fact find, or the reverse, is the switch's starting position being wrong.

comparison.tolerance: Each dimension the report compares must be supported by provider or research documentation.
falsePositiveGuards: Provider fund-range and option data changes over time; check the date of the research before treating a difference as an error.
Where the existing scheme is better on a dimension, the report must say so — a one-sided comparison is a finding in itself.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: a switch recommended with no comparison of what is being left behind.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Potential Concern: comparison asserted with no switch analysis or provider data on file.

queryGroups.requirement: Benefits and costs of switching, including where benefits outweigh higher costs

queries.text: this switch is in your best interests for the following reasons
cost of switching initial adviser charge deducted from the transfer
difference in annual charges between the existing plan and the recommended plan per plan
queries.note: Per-plan charge impact is the arithmetic against which the per-plan benefit claim is tested.

queries.text: exit penalty early surrender charge market value reduction on transfer
critical yield required growth to match the existing plan value

comparison.tolerance: Benefit claims must reconcile with the charge comparison for the same plan.
falsePositiveGuards: A benefit claimed at solution level may not hold for every ceding plan — test per plan, not in aggregate.
Higher cost is acceptable where the report explains why the benefits outweigh it; look for that explanation before flagging.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: costs of switching not disclosed.

queryGroups.requirement: Details of lost features and guarantees

queries.text: safeguarded benefits guaranteed annuity rate guaranteed minimum pension enhanced tax free cash
queries.note: Highest-severity group in the plan. Both a positive statement and an explicit negative ('does not contain any safeguarded benefits') are valid findings; silence is not.

queries.text: protected pension age protected tax free cash percentage above 25%
with profits bonus loyalty bonus terminal bonus lost on transfer
life cover waiver of premium or other benefits attached to the existing policy
policy schedule scheme booklet terms of the existing arrangement
employer contributions would be lost if you transfer away from the workplace scheme

falsePositiveGuards: An explicit 'no safeguarded benefits' statement in the report must still be corroborated by the policy documentation — the report asserting it is not evidence of it.
Absence of a guarantee in a policy summary is not proof of absence; look for the scheme booklet or provider confirmation.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: the report never addresses whether anything is being given up.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Potential Concern of the highest severity where a switch proceeds with no provider documentation confirming the absence of guarantees.

queries.text: leaving the existing scheme untouched or switching funds within the existing plan
consolidating into the employer scheme or another existing plan instead
why the alternative option was not recommended for this particular plan

falsePositiveGuards: Options assessed once for the whole case may legitimately cover several plans — check whether the rejection reasoning is plan-specific where the plans differ materially.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: switching recommended without considering leaving the plan in place.

queries.text: the new plan would need to outperform the existing plan by in the first year
effect of switching reduction in the projected value at retirement
annual saving from the switch in monetary terms for this plan
queries.note: Set against the initial fee attributable to the same plan; a saving that takes decades to repay the fee is a fair-value concern.

falsePositiveGuards: Non-financial benefits (access, servicing, risk alignment) can justify a net cost increase where the report argues it explicitly.

sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Assess on the report's own figures; note the absence of independent switch analysis.

queryGroups.requirement: Lost guarantees or benefits disadvantage the client

queries.text: value of the guarantee being given up and why it is not needed
cost of replacing the lost benefit elsewhere

falsePositiveGuards: Only applies where G9.3 identified a benefit actually being given up.

sufficiency.ifBothAbsent: Not applicable where no safeguarded benefits exist and that is evidenced.

queryGroups.requirement: Other alternatives provide better outcomes for the client

queries.text: an internal fund switch would achieve the same outcome at lower cost
the existing scheme already offers the features the client needs

falsePositiveGuards: Consolidation for its own sake is a valid client objective where the client asked for it — check CHK-002 objectives before treating simplification as an insufficient reason.

sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: No finding where the research supports the chosen route.

decision.noIssue: For every ceding plan the report compares existing against recommended, discloses the costs and benefits of switching, addresses safeguarded benefits and penalties, and considers alternatives — all corroborated by categories E and G.
decision.potentialConcern: Any ceding plan lacks a comparison, lost features or guarantees are unaddressed or unevidenced, switching costs are not disclosed, the claimed benefit contradicts the charge analysis, or no alternative to switching was considered.
decision.notApplicable: No plan is being switched, transferred, encashed or surrendered.
severityHints: Highest: safeguarded benefits given up with no analysis, or no provider documentation confirming none exist.
Highest: employer contributions lost on a transfer from a live workplace scheme without that being addressed.
High: a switch justified on cost savings that the report's own comparison table contradicts.
High: the largest ceding plan by value has no plan-specific cost/benefit analysis.
Moderate: alternatives considered case-wide but not for a materially different plan.
Low: comparison present but a minor dimension omitted.
